summary: John Vincent Bellezza is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He studied under Yungdrung Tenzin and Tshering Choephel, and held a post at the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2014).

John W. Pettit specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed undergraduate studies at Haverford College, conducted doctoral work under Robert A. F. Thurman, and studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Lal Mani Joshi, Gunapala Dharmasiri, and Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa.

John W. Schroeder works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Los Angeles Valley College and the University of Oregon under Hee-jin Kim and Don Levi, later teaching at Oregon, the College of Wooster, and St. Mary's College of Maryland.

John W. Spellman was an Indologist and historian who studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham from circa 1958 to 1960. He held academic posts at the University of Washington (circa 1964–1967) and as a professor at the University of Windsor (circa 1967–1997).

John Watson McCrindle was an Indologist and historian who earned his BA and LLD from the University of Edinburgh. His career included serving as principal of Doveton College and Patna College, professor at Krishnagar Government College, and fellow at the University of Calcutta.
John Wenger was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Bern in 1827 and earned a Doctor of Divinity from the University of Rhode Island by 1878.

John Whalen-Bridge is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Connecticut, UC Davis, and the University of Southern California before holding appointments at the University of the Ryukyus (1993–1998) and the National University of Singapore.

John Whaley Watson was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served in the Bombay Staff Corps, as president of the Rajasthik Court in Kathiawar (circa 1873–1886), and as a political agent for the Kathiawar Agency (1881–1889).

John William Neill was an Indologist educated at King's College London and the University of Edinburgh. He served as a fellow of the University of Calcutta, professor at University College London (1896–1917), and reader of Marathi at SOAS University of London.

John Wilson was an Indologist, linguist, and religious studies scholar educated at the University of Edinburgh. He served as president of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai, vice-chancellor of the University of Mumbai, and founded Wilson College, Mumbai.
John Zephaniah Holwell was an Indologist who studied surgery at Guy's Hospital from circa 1729 to 1732. He was elected a fellow of the Royal Society in 1767.

Join Saeki was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Jōchō Chihaya and at Sennyu-ji. He served at the University of Tokyo, the Japan Academy, Kangakuin, and held the leadership of Horyu-ji from 1903 to 1950.
Joji Fujii is a historian and Japanologist. He completed his studies at Kyoto University circa 1966 to 1974 and later held an academic post there from circa 1989 to 2011.

Jokai Hiraoka was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history who studied at Kyoto University and the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Shuchiin University and served as a professor at Otemae University from circa 1966 to 1993.

Jon Holt specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA from the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and a PhD from the University of Washington, and was appointed professor of Japanese at Portland State University in 2010.

Jon Kabat-Zinn, working in religious studies and medicine, studied at Haverford College and MIT. He trained with various Buddhist teachers, taught at the Insight Meditation Society, and was a professor of medicine at the University of Massachusetts Chan Medical School.

Jonardon Ganeri is a philosopher and Indologist who studied at Cambridge and Oxford under Bimal Krishna Matilal. He held posts at Nottingham, Liverpool, Sussex, NYU, and became the Bimal K. Matilal Distinguished Professor of Philosophy at the University of Toronto.

Jonathan A. Silk is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who completed his doctoral studies at the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez. He held academic appointments at Western Michigan, Yale, UCLA, and Leiden University.

Jonathan C. Gold is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religion. He studied at Amherst College and the University of Chicago, and has held teaching posts at the University of Vermont, Drew University, and Princeton University.

Jonathan Christopher Cleary was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed doctoral studies in East Asian Languages and Civilizations at Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi and taught as an instructor at Wesleyan University.
